correctness.rationale: Classify a dominating set by selected left/right counts: both >=2 contribute A_n(t)^2 with A_n=(1+t)^n−1−nt; a singleton on one side forces the corresponding missing-neighbor vertex on the other side, yielding two n t²(1+t)^(n−1) terms with n t² double-count overlap; exactly entire single side contributes two t^n. For n>=5, d2=n,d3=2n(n−1),d4=C(n,2)^2+2nC(n−1,2), giving d3²−d2d4=−n²(n−1)(n²−13n+8)/4<0 for all n>=13. The finite complementary orders n=2..12 are EXHAUSTIVELY checked by all integer coefficient minors, not extrapolated. Strict increase to middle uses upward-closed probability d_k/C(2n,k), and strict fall after n follows every (n+1)-set dominating, d_n=C(2n,n)−2n and central binomial gap. Total-dom polynomial A_n² is an earlier known identity, and log-concavity follows from convolution of nonnegative log-concave interval-supported sequences. Independently enumerated all labeled subsets for n=2..6 and checked integer minors up to n=60; finite testing is not the infinite sign proof.
residual_risks: The n<=12 portion is a complete finite integer certificate, not a single symbolic uniform positive inequality.
Ordinary and total domination use different closed/open neighborhood conditions; do not transfer polynomial identity from one to other.

value.rationale: The full ordinary domination coefficient sequence of a canonical regular bipartite graph family exhibits an exact and persistent log-concavity change at the natural order threshold 12/13, while staying strictly unimodal and contrasting with the already-known total-domination formula. This is a motivated graph-polynomial structural cutoff, not merely recomputation of OEIS A287063 total counts. The threshold is proved for the entire infinite family by a symbolic negative minor plus exhaustive finite positive interval.
residual_risks: Some of the ordinary enumerator is easily derived by casework and its t=1 specialization is already tabulated; value resides in complete coefficient-shape classification.

final_claim: For the matching-deleted balanced complete bipartite crown graph Cr_n with n>=2, the ordinary domination polynomial has the displayed exact coefficient formula and is log-concave exactly for 2<=n<=12; from n=13, the degree-three minor is negative, but for n>=4 ordinary coefficients remain strictly unimodal with unique mode n. The previously known total-domination polynomial stays log-concave for all n.
limitations: All integer n>=2; n=2 disconnected special case, n>=4 strict mode.
No claim for arbitrary regular bipartite graphs or global domination polynomial conjectures.
